subject: Reserved GPU queueing playbook & carve-in request — Blackridge
messages:
From: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@blackridge.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@blackridge.ai
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary 'carve-in' headroom and queueing playbook for nightly ETL spikes

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We went through the usage spikes with our infra team and have a narrowly recurring pattern that collides with Redwood's nightly batch work (roughly 02:00–06:00 UTC). We want to avoid tail-latency regressions for our customer-facing inference calls while still keeping the economics of a reserved pool.

Request summary: can Redwood support a narrow "carve-in" that pins 2 GPUs for Blackridge during a 30–90 minute window tied to burst traffic (we'd still keep our existing 8-GPU reserved pool during daytime), plus an operational playbook that defines queueing behavior, pre-warm KV cache steps, and a runbook for automated fallback to hosted variants if the carve-in can't be met?

Attached: proposed SOW that details load profile and preferred calendar windows, and a CSV of recent peaks.

Key asks from our procurement team: 1) explicit wording of how carve-in affects other tenants (fairness), 2) an SLA amendment that calls out p95 latency target for small payloads (<256 tokens) during the carve-in window, and 3) credits or remedial steps if carve-in availability drops below agreed threshold.

Can you point us to how Redwood would measure and validate the carve-in (trace ids, dashboard snapshots), and what the timeline looks like for adding this to our dedicated contract?

Best,
Ethan Morales
Head of Platform, Blackridge AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@blackridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary 'carve-in' headroom and queueing playbook for nightly ETL spikes

Hi Ethan —

Appreciate the detail and the load profile attachment. Looping in Ben (solutions) and David (SRE/ops) so we can scope feasibility and the operational controls. High-level: we do support targeted reservation adjustments and priority pinning in Dedicated, but the semantics (hard pin vs. soft carve-in) and fairness constraints vary by pool and region.

Ben — can you review the CSV and propose a playbook (pre-warm, KV cache warmup hooks, token sizing recommendations) and an acceptance test we can run in staging?

David — same ask on observability: what we will need from Blackridge (trace ids, sample request ids) and what Redwood will provide (Grafana snapshots, token-level latency histograms) to make the SLA measurable.

Ethan — we'll come back with a draft carve-in appendix and a proposed change to the reserved capacity section of your contract. Tentative timeline: technical scoping this week; SOW revision and ops runbook early next week; legal sign-off following that.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@blackridge.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary 'carve-in' headroom and queueing playbook for nightly ETL spikes

Ethan —

Quick technical read after reviewing the CSV. Short summary of a safe approach we can run in staging: 

- Carve-in model: implement a "soft carve-in" with two levels:
  1) Priority pinning for 2 GPUs (requests from Blackridge go to priority lanes on those GPUs). If utilization > 85% for > 10m, the system will invoke fallback policy.
  2) If a hard reservation is required (no fallback), we can reserve 2 GPUs exclusively for the requested window, but that increases cost and affects pool headroom for other tenants.

- Queueing playbook: 
  * Pre-warm: run a KV warmup job 20 minutes before the start of the window (we can trigger via API).
  * Connection ramp: throttle new long-run requests during the first 5 minutes to prevent head-of-line blocking.
  * Tail-smoothing: apply token-bounded generation cap for small payloads to keep p95 latency tight.

- Measurement & SLA: we can provide a Grafana panel with token-level p50/p95/p99 and per-request trace ids. For the carve-in appendix we recommend an availability target for the carve-in window (e.g., 99.5% carve-in availability per calendar month) plus a latency SLO at p95.

Questions for Blackridge:
1) Do you require hard exclusivity for the 2 GPUs? If yes, what's the budget delta you expect?
2) Can you provide a small set of sample trace ids for the busy window so we can validate observability?

If you prefer, we can prototype the pre-warm + priority lanes in our staging cluster next Wed (06/30) and run a 2-hour soak test.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@blackridge.ai>
Date: 2027-06-23T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary 'carve-in' headroom and queueing playbook for nightly ETL spikes

Folks —

Operational notes from an SRE perspective:

- Observability contract: we need trace ids + request time windows from Blackridge in order to compute an authoritative post-hoc report. Redwood will produce a signed PDF with Grafana snapshots and raw percentile tables for each carve-in event.

- Fairness & isolation: if we do soft priority pinning, we'll include an eviction policy that favors short-running inference requests over long-running batch jobs within the pinned GPUs. We'll also set a circuit-breaker that drops into hosted model variants automatically after a configurable error/latency threshold to protect other tenants.

- Acceptance tests:
  * Pre-warm verification (KV hit-rate > 90% within first 10m)
  * Latency load test (synthetic small-payload p95 < 120ms under the projected arrival rate)
  * Failover validation (verify requests route to hosted fallback with <300ms added latency during an enforced carve-in failure)

- Compliance note: any hard pinning that reduces our able capacity by >10% for the pool will require Ops approval and a small dedicated maintenance window—this is why soft carve-in is our recommended default.

I can run the staging soak with Ben's help next Wed; will require a one-hour sync with Blackridge to get test tokens and a short-lived API key.

David Kim
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@blackridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, procurement@blackridge.ai
Date: 2027-06-24T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary 'carve-in' headroom and queueing playbook for nightly ETL spikes — next steps

Ethan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary / next steps: 
1) Technical scoping complete: Redwood recommends soft carve-in with priority pinning and the pre-warm + tail-smoothing playbook (Ben/David will run staging test on 2027-06-30).
2) Acceptance criteria to include in the SOW: KV hit-rate verification, small-payload p95 < 120ms under the modeled load, and documented failover behavior to hosted variants.
3) Legal / procurement: we'll add a 1-page carve-in appendix to your reserved capacity contract that specifies availability target (proposed 99.5% per calendar month) and remedial credits (tiered credit schedule). Draft SOW attached for your review.
4) Action items: Blackridge to provide 3–5 sample trace ids + the named calendar windows you want pinned; Redwood to run staging soak 06/30 and produce an operations runbook for sign-off.

If procurement needs cost options for hard exclusivity vs. soft carve-in we can provide both — Ben, please attach the cost delta to the SOW draft.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
